method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Sheet 87 covers O/O 1/2/P/P 1/2 and sheet 88 covers P 1/2/Q/Q 1/2/R, so Ave P 1/2 is the only shared corridor; both plates print 'AVENUE P 1/2' in this gutter (repeated in each street band) and each prints the other's number beside it ('88' on sheet 87, '87' on sheet 88). The cross-street run changes hundred-block exactly here: sheet 87's block west of the avenue reads 1915/1917/1919/1921/1923 with evens 1916/1918/1920/1922/1924, repeated in all three street bands; sheet 88's block east of it starts the next hundred at 2001/2003/2005/2007/2009 with 2002/2004/2006/2008/2010. The avenue frontage runs interlock across the gutter: sheet 87's east block face carries the evens 4002,4004,...4024 (and 3902-3928 in the band above) while sheet 88's west block face carries the odds 4001,4003,...4027 (3901-3927 above) - the two sides of the same segments of Ave P 1/2.
note: Detection candidates (87: 2749/1750/752; 88: 574/1569/2565) are mid-block lines. '70'' is printed mid-avenue on both plates - native x 3129 on sheet 87, native x 171 on sheet 88 - agreeing with the face-derived centres (sheet 87 west face 3028 + 105 = 3133; sheet 88 east face 267 - 105 = 162); 3131 / 166 recorded. Sheet 88 also prints '35'' twice beside its neat line in this gutter, the half-width from the sheet boundary.
